title: Sloboda Ukraine
capsule: Sloboda Ukraine (Slobozhanshchyna) was a frontier region of the Russian tsardom settled primarily by Ukrainian Cossack refugees fleeing Polish-Lithuanian pressure from the 1630s onward, organized into five self-governing regimental districts — Kharkiv, Sumy, Okhtyrka, Ostrohozk, and Izium — whose settlers received tax exemptions (slobody) in exchange for military service against Crimean Tatar raids. The city of Kharkiv, founded c. 1654, became the principal urban center. Peter I curtailed Cossack autonomy after Mazepa's defection at Poltava (1709); Catherine II abolished the regimental structure in 1765, converting the region into the Sloboda Ukraine Governorate and later the Kharkov Governorate (1796), effectively ending its autonomous character.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The approximate extent of Sloboda Ukraine is documented from Russian administrative records and the regimental organization; precise borders with the Hetmanate, Don Cossack territory, and the open steppe were never formally delimited.
